name: TPS61220DCKR
title: TPS6122x: 0.7 V input synchronous boost converter, 5.5 µA quiescent current, SC-70
summary: TPS61220, TPS61221 and TPS61222 are synchronous boost converters for one, two or three NiMH, NiCd or alkaline cells, or one lithium-ion cell. They start into a load from 0.7 V, run from 0.7 V to 5.5 V in, and draw 5.5 µA typical with no load. A hysteretic current-mode loop holds the inductor ripple near 200 mA and goes discontinuous at light load. TPS61220 sets 1.8 V to 6 V with a divider on FB; TPS61221 gives 3.3 V and TPS61222 5 V. In shutdown the input passes to the output; protection covers output overvoltage, overtemperature and input undervoltage.
key_figures: 400 mA typ, 240 mA min (VOUT = 3.3 V, VIN = 1.2 V, 25 °C)

notes: TPS61220 has an adjustable output, TPS61221 a fixed 3.3 V output and TPS61222 a fixed 5 V output; all three come in the 6-pin SC-70 (DCK) package.
An R suffix orders a reel of 3000 and a T suffix a reel of 250.
An Enhanced Product version, TPS61222-EP, exists for defense, aerospace and medical use.

circuits.title: Simplified schematic, adjustable output
circuits.description: TPS61220 raising an input between 0.7 V and VOUT to an output set between 1.8 V and 6 V; the 4.7 µH inductor runs from the input to the switch pin L; the output divider R1 over R2 feeds FB; EN is strapped to VIN so the converter runs whenever input is present. 10 µF ceramics hold the input and output.
notes: The adjustable design example uses R1 = 1.2 MΩ and R2 = 160 kΩ for 4.25 V.

circuits.title: Fixed output voltage supply
circuits.description: A fixed-output TPS6122x; the design example uses TPS61222 for a 5 V rail of up to 60 mA from two AA alkaline cells at better than 90 % efficiency. FB goes straight to VOUT because the divider is inside the part. EN is tied to VIN, the 4.7 µH inductor runs from VIN to L, and 10 µF ceramics sit at the input and output pins.
notes: The same circuit serves TPS61221 for a 3.3 V output.

circuits.title: Variable output voltage supply
circuits.description: TPS61220 giving 4.2 V at up to 50 mA from two AA alkaline cells at better than 80 % efficiency. R1 from VOUT to FB over R2 from FB to ground sets the output against the 500 mV feedback level: 1.2 MΩ over 160 kΩ gives 4.25 V before tolerances. EN is tied to VIN; L1 and the two 10 µF ceramics are as in the fixed-output circuit.
notes: R1 and R2 come from the output-voltage equation with VFB = 500 mV.

circuits.title: Parameter measurement circuit
circuits.description: The circuit the typical characteristics are taken in: any TPS6122x with EN tied to VIN, a 4.7 µH inductor from VIN to L, 10 µF X5R ceramics at input and output, and the R1/R2 divider to FB. On the adjustable part R1 and R2 set the output; on a fixed part R1 is 0 Ω and R2 is left off.

operation.text: A synchronous boost: two low-on-resistance MOSFETs inside the part, a main switch from L to ground and a rectifying switch from L to VOUT, both actively driven. Fixed-voltage versions carry their feedback divider inside; TPS61220 uses an outside one on FB.

The controller holds the inductor's peak-to-peak ripple at about 200 mA and moves the level of that ripple up or down with the load. An error amplifier compares the fed-back output with the internal reference and sets the level. When the load needs less average current than the fixed ripple delivers, the inductor current turns discontinuous, which keeps light-load efficiency up. The loop oscillates by itself, is inherently stable, answers load steps quickly and tolerates a broad range of L and C values.

EN high runs the converter; EN low stops switching and turns off all the control circuitry. In shutdown the rectifying MOSFET's body diode still links input to output, so VOUT sits at up to the input voltage, lower under load. The input draws 0.2 µA typical in shutdown.

Once EN goes high the part starts. If the input is too low to run the control circuit, a start-up oscillator drives the switches at its own frequency with a reduced current limit. When the output reaches about 1.8 V the control circuit takes over and normal hysteretic operation begins. The start-up time varies with the load and the input voltage. The part starts from 0.7 V into a load of 150 Ω or more.

At the switch current limit, the main switch opens so the input current climbs no further, and the output sags. If the output falls below the input, the rectifying switch's body diode conducts; that diode stays on, and only the circuit's DC resistance limits that current. Once the overload is removed the set output returns.
The converter stops when the input falls below the lockout threshold, 0.5 V typical and 0.7 V maximum on a falling input.

The output is also watched internally. If feedback is lost and VOUT climbs to the internal limit, typically 6.5 V, the voltage amplifier clamps the output there. In an LED driver this guards the circuit when an LED fails.
An on-chip sensor stops the part when the junction passes about 140 °C and lets it run again once it has cooled; 20 °C of hysteresis prevents chatter around the threshold.

The family runs from a stack of one, two or three NiMH, NiCd or alkaline cells (0.7 V to 5.5 V), from one lithium-ion or lithium-polymer cell (2.5 V to 4.2 V), or from any source in the 0.7 V to 5.5 V range. Solar cells and supercapacitors are also usable within the recommended operating conditions. A lower input gives a lower maximum output current and somewhat lower efficiency.

The inductor goes between VIN and L. 4.7 µH performs well across the full range of input and output voltage. A larger value lowers the switching frequency and the switching losses and so can raise efficiency; values under 2.2 µH are not recommended. Rate the inductor for the peak current of the peak-current equation, allowing for load steps and faults. Series used with the part: Coilcraft EPL3015 and EPL2010, Murata LQH3NP, Taiyo Yuden NR3015, Würth WE-TPC Typ S.
A ceramic of 10 µF or more, mounted right beside the VIN and GND pins, helps transient response and EMI.

Use small ceramics placed tight against VOUT and GND: 4.7 µF at least, 10 µF recommended. With an inductor above 4.7 µH, the output capacitance in µF must be at least half the inductance in µH. If a large capacitor has to sit away from the IC, put a ceramic of about 2.2 µF in parallel right at the pins. ESR does not affect stability, but low-ESR parts keep ripple down; more capacitance reduces dips on fast load steps.

The divider runs VOUT to FB to GND and regulates FB at 500 mV typical. Keep the divider current about 100 times the 0.01 µA FB current, which means R2 under 500 kΩ for 1 µA or more. The output should be set no higher than 6.0 V. On the fixed versions FB connects straight to VOUT.

Route the power current loop and the power ground short and wide, and put the input capacitor, output capacitor and inductor right at the IC. On TPS61220 place the divider near the GND pin and return its ground on its own short trace apart from power ground, the two meeting close to the GND pin, so power current does not shift the feedback reference. TI's example layout for the adjustable part has C1 beside VIN, C2 beside VOUT, L1 above the IC, and R1 and R2 below it by FB.
How much the part can dissipate depends on the system: board copper, the thermal coupling from package to board, air flow and nearby heat sources all change it. RθJA is 231.2 °C/W.
